rows.title: Statistics Canada reports retail sales up 0.8 per cent in September at $75.3B
rows.summary: Statistics Canada said retail sales rose 0.8% to $75.3 billion in September, but most of the gain came from higher prices at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, where sales jumped 6.9%. Measured in volume, which strips out price changes, total retail sales grew only 0.1%. Core retail sales, which leave out gas stations and car and parts dealers, also rose just 0.1%. General merchandise and clothing stores gained, while food and beverage retailers saw sales slip 0.4%. StatCan's early estimate points to a 1.5% drop in October, a sign that consumer spending may be weakening as fuel costs squeeze household budgets.
rows.fact: Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% to $75.3 billion in September, led by a 6.9% jump at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. Sales volume and core retail sales each rose only 0.1%, and food and beverage sales fell 0.4%.
rows.outlook: StatCan's advance estimate suggests October retail sales fell 1.5%, though the agency says that figure will be revised.
rows.why: 매출액(명목)과 판매량(실질)의 차이를 통해, 물가가 오르면 소비가 늘어난 것처럼 보이지만 실제로 사는 물건은 거의 늘지 않을 수 있다는 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: By comparing sales in dollars with sales in volume, it shows how rising prices can make spending look stronger even when people are barely buying more.
rows.term_def: Nominal sales count the dollars spent, so they rise when prices rise. Real or volume sales remove the effect of price changes to show how much more stuff people actually bought.
rows.note: Released 8:30 a.m. ET Nov. 20 (22:30 KST). Key figures cross-checked with the Reuters report and Retail Insider's account of the StatCan release; Reuters adds that August was revised up to +1.4%.

opinion.title: Canada's retail sales rose to $75.3 billion in September on higher gasoline station receipts
opinion.author: The Hub Staff
opinion.summary: The Hub's analysis argues that September's gain mostly reflects what Canadians paid for fuel rather than how much they bought, since volume and core sales each rose only 0.1%. It notes that the October advance estimate of -1.5% is based on responses from only about 58% of surveyed firms, so it could change when revised data come out on Dec. 18. Economist Trevor Tombe estimates gasoline is about 3% of household spending and that a lasting 50% oil price rise would cost a typical household close to $1,000 a year. The piece also cites warnings that a large federal deficit leaves little room for stimulus without risking more inflation. It concludes that higher energy prices are hitting an economy that was already weak.
opinion.why: 기름값 상승이 가계 소비와 경제 전체에 어떤 부담을 주는지, 그리고 예비 통계를 왜 조심해서 읽어야 하는지를 함께 보여주는 해설입니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains how rising fuel prices weigh on household spending and the wider economy, and why early estimates should be read with caution.

rows.title: Consumer mood improves, but is it just a post-election 'sugar high'?
rows.summary: The University of Michigan's final consumer sentiment index for November rose to 51.5 from 48 in October, about a 7% gain, after hitting a record low this spring. Survey director Joanne Hsu said the midterm election results, falling gas prices and stock market turbulence all shaped the reading, with consumers expecting policy changes and possible tariff rollbacks. Inflation expectations fell sharply, and lower-wealth households reported better finances thanks to cheaper gasoline, while people with the most stock holdings said their finances worsened. Even so, the index is still about 20 points below where it stood when President Trump's second term began, and affordability remains the top worry. Experts quoted in the article warn the boost could fade once holiday credit card bills arrive.
rows.fact: The University of Michigan sentiment index rose to 51.5 in November from 48 in October, based on interviews from Oct. 20 to Nov. 16. Business-condition expectations rose after the election, inflation expectations fell, and lower-wealth consumers gained most from falling gas prices.
rows.outlook: GWU's Todd Belt suggested the lift may be a post-election 'sugar high' that drops off when holiday credit card bills come due.
rows.why: 사람들의 기대(심리)가 소비와 물가에 영향을 준다는 점, 그리고 선거나 기름값 같은 사건이 경제 심리를 어떻게 바꾸는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how people's expectations can shape spending and inflation, and how events like elections and gas prices shift economic mood.
rows.term_def: A survey-based score of how confident households feel about their finances and the economy. Higher readings often mean people are more willing to spend, which drives much of economic growth.
rows.note: Final November reading released 10 a.m. ET Nov. 20 (00:00 KST Nov. 21). Headline 51.5 and the fall in one-year inflation expectations to 3.7% cross-checked with Yahoo Finance's report.

opinion.title: Consumer Sentiment Gets a Post-Election Lift as Inflation Expectations Plunge
opinion.author: Neil Sethi
opinion.summary: Sethi digs into the details of the November survey: the expectations index rose to 52.9, its highest since July, while current conditions improved more modestly to 49.4. One-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.7%, the largest one-month drop since June 2025, and long-run expectations eased to 3.3%. Independents drove much of the change, while Republicans' expectations fell sharply, narrowing the partisan gap. He notes the survey closed before a sharp stock sell-off on Nov. 20 and argues the mood would likely look worse now. Pointing to past episodes, he adds that big drops in inflation expectations have often continued for another month.
opinion.why: 인플레이션 기대가 왜 중앙은행에 중요한지, 그리고 같은 통계라도 세부 항목과 시점을 따져 봐야 한다는 점을 보여줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows why inflation expectations matter to central banks and why it pays to look at the details and timing behind a headline number.

rows.title: Foreigners continue to offload Korean stocks in Oct.
rows.summary: Data from the Financial Supervisory Service show foreign investors sold a net 25.97 trillion won (about $19.5 billion) of Korean stocks in October, after net selling of 19.11 trillion won in September. US investors were the biggest sellers at about 15.9 trillion won, followed by Asian investors. At the same time, foreigners bought a net 7.63 trillion won of Korean bonds, so money moved from riskier stocks into safer debt rather than leaving entirely. Foreign stock holdings fell to 1,899 trillion won, or 34% of market value, while foreign bond holdings reached 330.3 trillion won, 11.3% of listed bonds. The report points to geopolitical risks and doubts about whether AI spending will pay off as the backdrop.
rows.fact: Foreigners net sold 25.97 trillion won of Korean stocks in October, the second straight month of heavy selling, with US investors selling the most. They net bought 7.63 trillion won of Korean bonds, lifting foreign bond holdings to 330.3 trillion won.
rows.why: 외국인 투자자들이 주식에서 채권으로 돈을 옮기는 '자본 이동'이 한국 금융시장과 환율에 어떤 영향을 주는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It helps you think about how capital flows, such as foreigners moving money from stocks to bonds, affect Korea's financial markets and currency.
rows.term_def: Money moving across borders to buy assets such as stocks and bonds. When foreign investors sell a country's stocks and take money home, it can push down share prices and weaken the currency.
rows.note: Official FSS monthly data. Figures cross-checked with the Korea Herald's Nov. 21 report (25.98 trillion won stock sales; 7.38 trillion won net bond purchase after maturities, versus 7.63 trillion won gross). Not covered earlier this week.

opinion.title: Record profits but record outflows: 'Sell Korea' trade stalks Seoul market
opinion.author: Gregor Stuart Hunter and Heekyong Yang
opinion.summary: This Reuters analysis explains a puzzle: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are posting record profits, yet foreign investors are pulling money out of Korea at a record pace. It reports that foreigners are on track for a seventh straight month of net selling, with cumulative outflows of about $115 billion, the largest in LSEG data going back to 2008. Worries that the AI boom is peaking, the unwinding of leveraged ETFs and slowing company buybacks have amplified the slide. Korean stocks now look cheap compared with world markets on a price-to-earnings basis. Some analysts call it a full 'Sell Korea' trend, while others, including Goldman Sachs and CLSA, argue the chip earnings outlook for 2027 remains solid.
opinion.why: 기업 실적이 좋아도 투자자 심리와 글로벌 자금 흐름 때문에 주가가 떨어질 수 있다는 점, 그리고 반도체에 집중된 한국 경제의 위험을 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that stock prices can fall even when profits are strong, because of investor sentiment and global money flows, and highlights the risk of Korea's heavy reliance on chips.

rows.title: UK retail sales beat forecasts after government tells households to stock up
rows.summary: Official ONS data showed British retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October, beating every forecast in a Reuters poll, and annual growth picked up to 2.3%. The ONS said supermarkets reported higher sales of long-life food such as tinned goods and UHT milk after the government's 'Be Ready' campaign urged households to keep three days of emergency supplies. Cooler weather also lifted clothing sales after a warm September. The data arrive as UK inflation has hit a one-year high of 3.6% and the Bank of England has raised interest rates for the first time in three years. Economists said the jump gave few clues about whether spending will stay strong, especially with energy bills set to rise.
rows.fact: UK retail sales volumes rose 0.7% month on month in October and 2.3% year on year, beating all forecasts in a Reuters poll. Food store volumes rose 0.8%, helped by stockpiling of long-life goods after government emergency-preparedness advice.
rows.outlook: The EY ITEM Club's Matt Swannell expects energy prices to rise by more than 20% in January, making next year difficult for retailers that don't sell essentials.
rows.why: 정부의 안내 한 가지가 소비 통계를 일시적으로 끌어올릴 수 있다는 점을 통해, 경제 지표를 해석할 때 '일회성 요인'을 구분하는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a single government message can temporarily lift spending data, teaching you to separate one-off factors when reading economic statistics.
rows.term_def: A temporary event, such as a holiday, unusual weather or a stockpiling rush, that pushes a statistic up or down for a short time without changing the underlying trend.
rows.note: ONS release 07:00 GMT Nov. 20 (16:00 KST). Cross-checked with the PA report via LBC, which adds that September was revised to -0.6% and economists had expected a 0.1% fall. Distinct from the BRC sales monitor and UK inflation stories covered earlier.

opinion.title: UK retail sales jump 0.7% in October as shoppers stockpile essentials
opinion.outlet: City AM / Business Live (via AOL UK)
opinion.author: Felix Armstrong
opinion.summary: This piece gathers expert reactions to the October figures, which showed a 0.7% rise after a 0.6% fall in September. MHA's Rajeev Shaunak argues the stockpiling boost is probably a one-off that hides real problems for retailers, since squeezed budgets leave little room beyond essentials. He adds that a Black Friday rush for discounts would not be the same as a true recovery in demand. Lloyds' Sandra Prince also calls it a possible short-term spike. GfK's Neil Bellamy notes consumer confidence improved slightly in November to -22 but remains fragile.
opinion.why: 좋은 통계 뒤에 숨은 약한 소비 수요를 전문가들이 어떻게 읽어내는지 보여주어, 숫자만 보고 판단하지 않는 습관을 기르게 해 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how experts read weak underlying demand behind a strong headline number, building the habit of not judging by the figure alone.

rows.title: China's loan prime rates remain unchanged
rows.summary: China kept its one-year loan prime rate at 3% and its over-five-year rate, which guides mortgages, at 3.5%, leaving them unchanged for the 18th month in a row since June 2025. Average rates on new corporate loans in October were about 2.9%, roughly 0.2 points lower than a year earlier, while new mortgage rates held at about 3.1%. Instead of a broad rate cut, the central bank has used targeted tools, including cutting a lending facility rate to 1.5%, adding 700 billion yuan in relending quotas for tech, farming and small firms, and introducing interest subsidies for some first-time homebuyers. The PBOC's latest quarterly report also says loan pricing will move from relying on a single LPR toward a more diversified set of benchmarks. Analysts say firmer growth, including 4.5% third-quarter GDP growth, reduces the urgency of broad cuts.
rows.fact: The one-year LPR stayed at 3% and the over-five-year LPR at 3.5%, unchanged for 18 straight months. October's average new corporate loan rate was about 2.9% and the new mortgage rate about 3.1%.
rows.outlook: Golden Credit Rating's Wang Qing expects recent targeted measures to enter an observation period, keeping the LPR stable in the near term.
rows.why: 금리를 전체적으로 내리는 대신 특정 분야에만 돈을 공급하는 '선별적 통화정책'이 무엇인지, 그리고 중국 경제의 고민을 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It explains targeted monetary policy, which channels money to specific sectors instead of cutting rates for everyone, and the challenges facing China's economy.
rows.term_def: China's benchmark lending rate, based on quotes from major banks and guided by the central bank. Banks use it to set interest rates on business loans and mortgages.
rows.note: Rates match other wire reports (Investing.com, Seeking Alpha). Reuters reports the PBOC shifted its main policy rate to an overnight rate this month; the Xinhua piece does not cover that detail. Not covered earlier this week.

opinion.title: China expected to hold benchmark lending rates in November, but some see a cut coming
opinion.author: Reuters Shanghai Newsroom
opinion.summary: Written the day before the decision, this Reuters piece surveyed 28 market participants, 23 of whom correctly expected no change in the LPR. It explains that the PBOC formally moved its main policy rate to an overnight lending rate this month, which effectively lowered the floor of its rate framework by 15 basis points. The central bank also plans to make loan pricing less dependent on the LPR by adding the overnight rate as another reference. Citi analysts saw a November cut as implausible but expect two 10-basis-point cuts in 2027. Others argue more stimulus may still be needed because factory output slowed and consumer spending stayed weak in October.
opinion.why: 중앙은행이 기준금리 체계 자체를 바꾸는 이유와, 전문가들이 앞으로의 금리를 어떻게 예측하는지 엿볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It gives a look at why a central bank would change its policy rate framework and how experts forecast where rates are heading.
